Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-19
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto transcript
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood CSM), Jordan Malik (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Stratus Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Stratus DevOps Lead), Carmen Ruiz (Stratus Security)

Summary:
Quick handoff from onboarding to launch readiness. Confirmed network and security checklist, clarified dedicated vs hosted for initial pilot, agreed to load test cadence, and set action items for SSO, VPC peering, and data retention. Some transcription glitches and spotty audio during Liam's connection hop.

Topics:
- Network/VPC peering and egress rules
- SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping
- Hosting mode: Dedicated reserve vs hosted with private routing
- Pre-warm and autoscaling behavior for launch day
- Benchmarks: p50/p95 latency goals and acceptable cost per 1K tokens
- Security: KMS options, SOC2 evidence, audit log retention

Action items (recap):
- See metadata action_items list above; also in body below.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time today. Quick rollcall, I'll start — Avery from Redwood, I'm the CSM on this account.
[00:06] Priya: Hi all, Priya here. Head of Platform at Stratus. Liam and Carmen are on as well.
[00:11] Liam: Hey. Sorry, had to jump networks, might be a bit echoey.
[00:14] Carmen: Carmen here, security.
[00:16] Jordan: Jordan, solutions engineer from Redwood. We'll run the technical checklist after the high level.

[00:28] Avery: Cool — goal for today is a handoff focused on launch readiness: network, security, and a plan for the first load test and cutover. We have about an hour, so should be able to nail down owners and dates. Any additional stakeholders we should loop in?
[00:36] Priya: Not right now. We'll loop in our infra lead if needed for the peering.

[01:02] Jordan: Great. I'll start with a concise rundown of the hosting options you flagged in the RFP — you guys had asked about Dedicated vs Hosted with private routing? I'll clarify tradeoffs.
[01:16] Jordan: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity — predictable throughput and lower jitter. Hosted is faster to get started and we can pin model versions, but you may hit multi-tenant rate limits unless you use a private routing / Dedicated-like commit. For regulated data we often recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated depending on isolation needs.
[01:36] Priya: We're leaning toward Dedicated for the first 6 months to control latency for transaction scoring, but we want to understand the network setup and KMS integration.
[01:45] Carmen: Right — encryption at rest and in transit, HSM/KMS options, and audit logs retention are the big ones for us. Also SSO mapping for RBAC.

[02:05] Jordan: On KMS, we support customer-managed keys — you can bring your own KMS (AWS KMS / Cloud HSM). For Private deployments we also support an on-prem HSM path. Audit logs are configurable; we'll expose request-level traces for your ops. I'll send the compliance packet after this call (link: https://redwood.in/security-pack).

[02:37] Priya: Thanks. On audit logs: how long do you retain by default? We may need 12 months for certain transaction audit trails.
[02:45] Jordan: Default retention for hosted is 90 days, but for Dedicated/Private customers we can extend retention as an add-on. We'll include configurable retention options in the runbook.

[03:10] Avery: I'll own the next steps for the compliance docs; Carmen, if you send a list of any additional evidence you need (SOC scope, pen test artifacts), we'll coordinate with our security team.
[03:20] Carmen: Will do. Expect a short list by end of day Friday.

[03:44] Liam: Quick infra question — for the Dedicated pool, do we have control over the subnet egress IPs? We need stable IPs for our firewall allowlist.
[03:52] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated can be deployed into your VPC with predictable egress via NAT gateways or through a transit; we can provide the per-AZ pool IP ranges for allowlisting. For hosted public endpoints, IP ranges are larger and less stable.

[04:18] Priya: OK, practical ask — send a VPC peering guide and the exact egress ports/protocols to open. Liam will coordinate.
[04:23] Avery: Noted — action: Avery to share VPC peering guide.

[04:40] [audio glitch] Liam: Sorry, saying that we'll need both outbound and inbound rules for the private endpoint? I heard inbound only, hold on —
[04:48] Jordan: We support both approaches: Private endpoints in your VPC or our side with peering. We'll include diagrams for both.

[05:10] Jordan: Moving on — rollout strategy. We recommend canary rollout with automatic fallback. Start with small traffic percentage on the Redwood Dedicated model, collect latency/cost metrics and quality evals, then expand. For transaction scoring use p95 latency < 500ms as a target for launch, but maybe aim for p50 ~120ms and p95 under 500ms depending on model size.
[05:40] Priya: Our SLA requires transactions under 400ms at p95 for the most critical flow. Can we meet that?
[05:47] Jordan: Depends on model selection and quantization. If you pick a smaller quantized variant we can hit lower latency. We'll run a benchmark with your payload to confirm.

[06:10] Priya: Payloads vary — average prompt ~180 tokens, with some longer ones up to 800. We'll share a traffic sample.
[06:18] Jordan: Please do. That will let us select the right kernel configs and batching policy. For 800-token long tails we should expect higher p95; caching and prefix KV caching can help for repeated context.

[06:44] Avery: Action: Stratus to provide sample traffic profile and peak QPS by 2027-02-25.

[07:08] Carmen: SSO — we will use Okta and need SAML mapping for groups to roles in Redwood. What's the workflow?
[07:15] Jordan: We have an SSO/SAML integration checklist. We'll provision a test SP and give you a test account; you map groups to Redwood roles. Avery will send the checklist and a short test plan.
[07:28] Avery: I'll get that out today.

[07:58] Liam: Regarding pre-warm: during batch loads do you support warm-up tokens and pre-warming to reduce cold-start latency?
[08:05] Jordan: Yes. We have pre-warm mechanisms for model kernels and we also support keep-alive/concurrency reservations on Dedicated pools. For warm-up we recommend a short burst of synthetic traffic before go-live.

[08:32] Priya: For launch day we want to avoid any cold start. Can Redwood coordinate a pre-warm window?
[08:38] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll schedule a pre-warm with your infra team — Jordan will coordinate and provide scripts.

[09:02] [15:34] Jordan: (jump ahead in recording log) Now on observability: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and tracing. You'll get a dashboard for the Dedicated pool. We'll also give you a webhook for alerts and a CSV export for billing reconciliation.

[09:28] Priya: Great — the finance team wants a predictable cost forecast. Can you provide cost-per-1k-token estimates for the model variants you recommend?
[09:36] Jordan: We'll produce that after the initial benchmark against your sample prompts. Estimates will include quantized vs fp16 differences.

[10:00] Priya: Any known competitors that do similar managed Dedicated pools? We just want to know the landscape.
[10:06] Avery: Anthropic and AWS (Bedrock) are often mentioned; Cohere does inference managed offerings too, but the differences are in the runtime opitimiz—opti—(laughs) implementation, and the tooling for rollout and observability. We can share a short competitor brief.

[10:30] [11:12] Carmen: On auditability — you said request-level traces; does that include the full prompt text in the logs?
[11:19] Jordan: By default we redact prompt text in audit logs for hosted tiers; for Dedicated/Private you can choose to keep plaintext traces but that's on the customer to manage and secure. We recommend token-level metadata and hashes in the default logs, with option to store full text in a customer-managed S3 with KMS.

[11:46] Carmen: Ok that matches our compliance posture — we will likely require prompt hashing and only store full text behind our KMS.

[12:05] Priya: Any limitations on model rollout across regions? We need low-latency for EU clients as well.
[12:12] Jordan: You can deploy Dedicated pools in multiple regions. Smart routing can send EU traffic to EU pools to keep latency low. There's some replication cost for model weights across pools. We'll include a multi-region cost estimate in the benchmarking doc.

[12:40] Liam: About preflight tests — can SEs run a synthetic load test that mimics our peak QPS?
[12:47] Jordan: Yes, SEs can run load tests against a staging endpoint. We prefer a test window where you throttle production and give us a target QPS. We'll need an agreed test plan.

[13:10] Avery: Action: Jordan to prepare load-test plan and dev-config for private deployment — due 2027-02-28.

[13:34] [13:45] Priya: A few practicalities — our platform uses an internal tracing header that we pass through; is there a passthrough for distributed tracing?
[13:51] Jordan: Yes — we support common tracing headers (W3C traceparent, x-request-id). We'll pass those through so your tracing correlates end-to-end.

[14:14] Liam: One more network question — for egress costs, if we peer and host in our VPC will egress go through our NAT? Any surprises in billing?
[14:23] Jordan: If you host the Dedicated pool in your VPC, you control egress billing. For hosted endpoints there may be egress costs from Redwood's cloud provider. We'll document the options and sample cost math.

[14:46] Priya: Thanks. Also want to clarify backups — model artifacts: will Redwood manage model version storage or do we need to keep copies?
[14:54] Jordan: We manage the storage for model binaries in our registry but give you version pins. For DR you can request exportable model snapshots — we'll include export steps in the runbook.

[15:20] [15:30] Carmen: For SOC2 evidence — do you have a standard attestation packet or an SSP?
[15:36] Jordan: Yes, Redwood provides an SSP + SOC2 report for enterprise customers under NDA. Avery will coordinate the exchange.

[15:58] Priya: Great. We're trying to lock a timeline — target pilot start the week of 2027-03-08, with a 2-week pilot then go/no-go for full launch. Is that realistic?
[16:07] Jordan: That gives ~2.5 weeks to run benchmarks and a load test if you share traffic samples this week. We can probably make it if the infra items are quick.

[16:30] Liam: Can we do an initial pilot in hosted but with private routing to speed things up while you provision Dedicated?
[16:37] Jordan: Yes — many customers do hosted private routing as a stopgap. It reduces setup time. You lose some isolation guarantees vs Dedicated but it's much quicker.

[16:58] Priya: Let's tentatively do hosted private routing for pilot and stand up Dedicated for production. We'll finalize after the benchmark.

[17:12] Avery: Noted. Action: Stratus to confirm pilot hosting choice by 2027-02-22.

[17:36] [18:01] Jordan: A few notes on observability and regression detection — Redwood Optimize can run quality monitoring against a prompt set and alert on regressions post-rollout. If you want we can onboard a baseline eval set (we call it an eval-suite) and tie alerts to the console.

[18:20] Priya: Yes please. We'll prepare a small eval set from our historical transactions (sanitized).

[18:44] Carmen: On encryption key rotation — are there any windows where rekeying will cause latency spikes?
[18:51] Jordan: No impact on inference latency; key rotation is at storage/envelope level. We will coordinate rotation windows with your security team.

[19:12] Priya: Ok. Anything else for the launch checklist?
[19:16] Avery: I'll read the top-level checklist items: VPC peering docs, SSO/SAML mapping, sample payloads, load-test plan, KMS decision, and compliance evidence. We have owners and target dates in the action items above.

[19:38] Liam: One oddity — during earlier POC our token billing view was off by around 6% compared to our internal meter; is that expected?
[19:47] Jordan: We saw small discrepancies before due to tokenization differences and how white space is counted. We'll sync offline with our billing ops and share reconciliation guidance.

[20:05] Priya: Good. Recap next steps?
[20:09] Avery: Recap: Avery sends SSO checklist and VPC peering guide by 2027-02-22/23; Jordan prepares load-test plan by 2027-02-28; Stratus (Liam) shares infra diagram and egress rules by 2027-02-24; Carmen sends compliance evidence list by EOD Friday; Stratus sends sample traffic by 2027-02-25. We schedule the load test for the week of 2027-03-01.

[20:42] Priya: Sounds right. Anything else?
[20:46] Jordan: Quick note — I'll attach a small script that simulates typical prompt lengths (small/medium/long) so you can run local checks.

[21:00] [audio] Liam: Sorry, I lost audio for a bit — can you repeat the pilot hosting recommendation?
[21:07] Avery: Sure — pilot in hosted with private routing, production on Dedicated.

[21:26] Priya: One last question from finance — are there minimum commit terms for Dedicated?
[21:32] Avery: Yes Dedicated is typically a reserved monthly commit (we can do monthly or annual). We'll include options in the pricing sheet.

[21:50] Priya: Okay. Good to move forward. We'll reconvene after the documents are exchanged.

[22:12] Carmen: Thanks all.
[22:15] Jordan: Thanks, everyone — I'll send the technical packet and load-test plan.
[22:20] Avery: Meeting end — I'll follow up with the runbook and next steps.
